description: Follow-up of defk-ktw. An alloc skips zeroing only for: x = alloc(e, k * n), then (statements that do not mention x) a plain for i <- 0..(n - 1)//1 that writes x[k * i + c] for every c at the top level of its body. Kernels it misses, all still zeroed (in strips): encode64 (the loop plus an if-tail writes the last quad), resize_bilinear's out (out[(y * out_w + x) * ch + c] over nested loops), and monte_carlo draws/uniforms (a for ..., reduce: that writes out[i]). Skipping the memset saved 12-23% on scale and encode16 (under load). Any extension must stay sound and be checked against the brute-force shape test in test/alloc_unzeroed_test.exs.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Skip zeroing an alloc in more shapes where every element is provably written before it is read: reduce loops, a loop plus a tail, and 2-D index loops

**Current behavior:**
An alloc skips its memset only for: `x = alloc(e, k * n)`, then statements not mentioning x, then a plain `for i <- 0..(n - 1)//1` writing `x[k * i + c]` for every c at the top level of its body. Still zeroed: encode64 (loop plus an if-tail writing the last quad), resize_bilinear's out (`out[(y * out_w + x) * ch + c]` in nested loops), monte_carlo draws/uniforms (a for-reduce writing out[i]). Skipping the memset saved 12-23% on scale and encode16 (provisional).

**Desired behavior:**
Extend the full-write proof to, in order of value (stop where soundness gets hard and say why):
1. A for-reduce over `0..(n - 1)//1` whose body writes x[k * i + c] for every c unconditionally (x may be the accumulator or a captured array).
2. A covering loop followed by a tail (straight-line or under an if whose every taken path writes) that writes exactly the remaining elements.
3. Nested range loops writing a row-major index `(y * w + x) * ch + c` covering 0..len-1, when the alloc length is the product of the loop extents.
Soundness rule: an element may be left unzeroed only if every path writes it before any read, raise or yield-visible escape; a raise before the full write must not expose unzeroed memory to Elixir (the array is freed, not returned).

**Key interfaces:**
- The unzeroed-alloc analysis and its report note; the brute-force shape test in the alloc-unzeroed test file

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Each supported shape has a positive test (no memset in the C / report says unzeroed) and near-miss negatives (a skipped element, a conditional write, a read before write, an early raise) that stay zeroed
- [ ] The brute-force shape test covers the new shapes and passes
- [ ] encode64, resize_bilinear and monte_carlo examples (whichever shapes landed) skip the memset; before/after numbers in docs/performance.md (provisional if loaded)
- [ ] Agreement and forced-yield tests pass; `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Proofs needing relations between variables (defk-2mz); non-range loops

title: Unzeroed alloc: prove full writes for reduce loops, loops plus a tail, and 2-D indices
